subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: The Therac-25: When Software Kills
description: A fast breakdown of The Therac-25: When Software Kills for builders.

hook.text: The Therac-25 radiation machine overdosed six patients between 1985 and 1987. Three died from massive radiation burns.

buildup.text: Earlier Therac models had hardware safety interlocks. The Therac-25 replaced them with software — cheaper and simpler.

discovery.text: A race condition let operators set high-power mode while the beam filter was absent. Full-strength radiation hit patients.

twist.text: The manufacturer dismissed early reports, insisting the machine couldn't overdose. They blamed operator error repeatedly.

climax.text: The disaster reshaped software safety standards. Safety-critical software now requires independent review and redundant checks.

punchline.text: Software replaced hardware safety. The software had a bug.

quiz.question: What critical design choice made the Therac-25 dangerous?
options: The machine used an experimental radiation source that was unstable
Hardware safety interlocks were replaced with software that had a race condition bug
The device was manufactured with substandard parts to reduce costs
